DELETE_TEMPLATE_COMMENT: <users>: who uses the deliverable, such as `the developer`. <achieve what>: what they achieve with it. <kind>: the kind of deliverable, such as `readme`. <ext>: the deliverable's own format, such as `md`. inputs: each kind of deliverable that this kind builds on. preconditions: each kind whose deliverables must pass before work on this kind starts. Each <kind> is the folder name of its best practice. Each list is empty where there's none.

critical_success_factors.DELETE_TEMPLATE_COMMENT: One for each thing that must go right for the users to reach the goal. <state>: the thing, as a state, in one sentence.

necessary_conditions.DELETE_TEMPLATE_COMMENT: One for each state of the deliverable that its critical success factor needs, with the practice that meets it. <section>: each heading of the template that holds the condition, as written there, or `the whole` where the whole deliverable holds it. <question>: the state, as a yes-or-no question about the deliverable. <gives>: what the condition gives the users. <source>: the practitioners' way of doing the work that the items follow, where N5 of the meta best practice has one named. Optional. Items: in the order, and each in the form, that N5 of the meta best practice gives them. at: `decide` or `make`. <item>: the decision, the step, or the check. <case>: when the item applies. Optional. trace: the tool call that shows the item done. Given only to an item that every run takes. <action>: `run` for a command, matched in full, `read` for a file read in full, or `write` for a file written. <take>: the command or the file's path, as the item writes it, with a value given at the start of the run written as `{<name>}`, such as `{deliverable}`. For `run` and `write`, any one of several `takes` shows the item done. For `read`, the item reads each of them in full.
